findings.title: Verify the installer before executing it as root
findings.whyItBreaks: The new RUN instruction follows redirects and streams the response directly to a root shell. If the installer content changes upstream, a fresh build can execute different commands and produce a different image without any repository change.

findings.title: Fail the build when the installer download fails
findings.whyItBreaks: If DNS resolution fails, curl exits nonzero without writing a script to stdout. The downstream sh receives empty input and exits zero. Docker uses the pipeline's final command status, so it marks the install step successful and proceeds to COPY even though the installer did not run. The -s flag also suppresses curl's diagnostic.

findings.title: Preserve the missing-key signal in LoadOrDefault
findings.whyItBreaks: Load returns an empty string with ErrMissing for an absent key and an empty string with nil for a present key whose value is empty. The new exported wrapper discards the error, so callers receive the same result in both cases.

findings.title: Complete result sends before Run returns
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously, every send completed before Run returned, in input order. With jobs [1] and a result channel buffered for one value, a caller can call Run and then close the channel. The new goroutine can reach the send after that close, causing a send-on-closed-channel panic. With multiple jobs, goroutine scheduling can also reorder results.

findings.title: Require both admin status and a matching tenant for deletion
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported deletion guard now returns true for a same-tenant non-admin and for an admin from another tenant. Both requests returned false before this change.

findings.title: Propagate parse failures before saving settings
findings.whyItBreaks: With stored settings `{"theme":"dark","fontSize":"14"}`, `parseSettings` previously threw before `updateFontSize` could call `save`. It now returns defaults, so updating the font size to 18 passes `{"theme":"light","fontSize":18}` to `save` and silently replaces the valid dark theme.

findings.title: Fetch artifacts from the commit named in the report
findings.whyItBreaks: When the requested branch and verified resolve to different commits, builtFrom identifies the requested branch's commit while artifacts lists files from the verified commit. The returned report associates those files with the wrong source commit.

findings.title: Apply the requested limit to recent entries
findings.whyItBreaks: renderFeed requests 20 entries at src/feed.ts:9. With 21 inputs, the changed return at src/feed.ts:5 supplies all 21. The copy loop at src/feed.ts:11 writes index 20, growing the output array to 21 elements.

findings.title: Count only the rows emitted in the manifest
findings.whyItBreaks: With one live entry and one stale entry, the renderer emits one data row but writes `# entry-count: 2` because the header still uses `entries.length`.

findings.title: Preserve the exported FormatLegacyID function
findings.whyItBreaks: The diff deletes ids.FormatLegacyID(int64) string at ids/format.go:9-11, so existing callers of the exported function fail to compile. FormatID requires a region and produces a different identifier format. The deleted assertion at ids/format_test.go:12 verifies that FormatLegacyID(42) returns LEG0000000042.

findings.title: Preserve the shippingQuote export from orders
findings.whyItBreaks: The base module exported shippingQuote. The new module imports quoteShipping for internal use and leaves shippingQuote unexported, so existing consumers that import shippingQuote from orders fail TypeScript compilation.

findings.title: Return 401 when the stored token hash is missing
findings.whyItBreaks: At app/token.py:10, hmac.compare_digest raises TypeError when the stored hash is None or a non-ASCII string. The previous equality check returned False for both inputs. The exception interrupts the condition at app/token.py:14 before the guard can return HTTP 401.

findings.title: Preserve indexed summation for arrays with custom iterators
findings.whyItBreaks: The new for...of loop consumes the array's Symbol.iterator when emitted as native JavaScript iteration. A number[] with indexed entries [1, 2] and an iterator that yields only 1 now returns 1. The base implementation reads both indexed entries and returns 3.

findings.title: Restore the uppercase result from execute
findings.whyItBreaks: A valid call such as execute("hello") previously returned "HELLO". It now throws Error("always fails"), so callers never receive the string result.

findings.title: Preserve read-only access for eligible viewers
findings.whyItBreaks: For an active viewer with 4 attempts, the base implementation returns "read-only". The new role check makes isEligible return false, so handle returns "rejected" at src/handler.ts:24 before reaching the read-only branch at src/handler.ts:25. That branch is now unreachable for every viewer.

findings.title: Require payment only when submitting an order
findings.whyItBreaks: The new payment check at src/policy.ts:7 makes canProceed return false for a draft with missing payment. The guard at src/actions.ts:9 therefore makes saveDraft return 'blocked' where it previously returned 'saved'.

findings.title: Read snapshot files from the requested channel’s commit
findings.whyItBreaks: When main and stable point to commits with different file lists, publishSnapshot(repo, "main") returns main’s commit and channel alongside stable’s files. The snapshot identifies the wrong commit as the source of its contents.

findings.title: Honor the requested limit when building items
findings.whyItBreaks: The new public limit parameter lets callers request a maximum number of items, but build("item", limit=1) returns ten because the loop uses the fixed max_count value.

findings.title: Reject nonpositive values in parse_positive_int
findings.whyItBreaks: The rename at src/validators.py:1 promises a positive integer, but int(value) accepts both "0" and "-1". charge uses the parsed value at src/validators.py:6 and returns -100 for "-1". total_cents(["2", "-1"]) returns 100 cents after accepting the invalid amount.

findings.title: Preserve the caller's DataFrame in apply_values
findings.whyItBreaks: For a row with key 'a' and value 1, applying {'a': 2} previously returned a separate DataFrame with value 2 while the input retained value 1. The changed assignment overwrites the input, so any caller holding a reference to it now sees value 2.

findings.title: Enforce positivity before calculating a charge
findings.whyItBreaks: The rename at src/parse.rs:1 introduces a positive-integer contract. The parser still returns -1 for "-1" and 0 for "0". The call at src/parse.rs:6 passes those values to multiplication at line 7, so charge returns -100 and 0 respectively.

findings.title: Remove the debug call that moves items before len()
findings.whyItBreaks: dbg!(items) moves the Vec<String> and returns it. The statement discards the return value, so items.len() on line 3 borrows a moved value and triggers Rust error E0382.

findings.title: Compute changed paths from the reported base revision
findings.whyItBreaks: When the pinned tag and latest resolve to different revisions, buildChangeset reports the pinned revision in fromRevision but computes changedPaths against latest. The returned list can omit paths that changed between those revisions, violating the documented contract that fromRevision identifies the revision used to compute changedPaths.

findings.title: Update the query to use the renamed column
findings.whyItBreaks: After migration 0002 succeeds, the SELECT email FROM users statement at src/query.sql:1 fails because users.email has been renamed to contact_email.

findings.title: Restore environment-based billing credentials
findings.whyItBreaks: Every call returns the committed credential-shaped literal. Deployments lose the ability to select or rotate the billing key through BILLING_API_KEY, and anyone with access to the commit can read the literal.

findings.title: Preserve the missing billing configuration error
findings.whyItBreaks: With BILLING_API_KEY unset or empty, the exported factory previously threw a configuration error. It now returns a BillingClient, so callers lose the error signal at construction.

findings.title: Restore the admin requirement for project purges
findings.whyItBreaks: For an archived project, a non-admin passes both guards, reaches db.delete(project.id), and receives "purged". An admin receives "forbidden" before the archive check. The base revision allowed deletion only for admins acting on archived projects.

findings.title: Restore the startup fallback for missing settings
findings.whyItBreaks: load_settings returns None for a nonexistent path or a file containing JSON null. With the fallback removed, startup subscripts None and raises TypeError instead of returning 1.

findings.title: Propagate gateway submission errors from Charge
findings.whyItBreaks: For a positive amount, Charge logs a non-nil error from Gateway.Submit and returns nil. Callers of the exported API lose the ability to distinguish a failed submission from a successful one or recover the underlying error with errors.Is.

findings.title: Keep cache entries scoped to each tenant
findings.whyItBreaks: After tenant A loads a setting, tenant B requesting the same name uses the same cache key. The cache hit returns A's value to B and skips the tenant-scoped store fetch.

findings.title: Preserve the two-argument invalidation API
findings.whyItBreaks: Existing TypeScript calls to invalidate(tenantId, name) fail type checking. Existing JavaScript callers still run, but the function treats tenantId as the setting name and leaves the intended cached value stale.

findings.title: Serialize reservations for the same SKU
findings.whyItBreaks: With one unit loaded, the first reserve call reads 1 and suspends in store.save(sku, 0) before updating the map. A second call reads the same 1 and also saves 0. When both saves resolve, both calls return true and the recorded stock reflects only one decrement.

findings.title: Preserve the backoff units consumed by job retries
findings.whyItBreaks: The retry loop at src/jobs/retry.ts:12 still multiplies backoff(a) by 1,000 before passing it to a millisecond timer. With the new return units, the first failure waits 1,000 seconds instead of 1 second, and the maximum wait rises from 30 seconds to 8 hours and 20 minutes.

findings.title: Propagate file close errors from Save
findings.whyItBreaks: If Flush succeeds and Close fails, the deferred call discards the close error and Save returns nil. The base implementation returned the close error to the caller.

findings.title: Include the last row of each page
findings.whyItBreaks: The page end is already exclusive. Subtracting 1 skips the final row of every nonempty page. At lib/pagination.py:40, render_page uses the shortened window. With rows ['a', 'b', 'c'] and page size 2, summarize emits only '1. a' and the page separator. Page size 1 drops every row.

findings.title: Preserve existing keyword arguments on pagination helpers
findings.whyItBreaks: The base signature accepts clamp(n=5, lo=0, hi=10) and returns 5. The new signature raises TypeError before entering the body. The same incompatibility affects page_count, page_window, render_page, and summarize through their renamed keyword parameters.

findings.title: Restore the cache TTL comparison
findings.whyItBreaks: With a 100 ms TTL, a first read at age 1 ms deletes the entry and returns null. A first read of an untouched entry at age 101 ms returns the expired value.

findings.title: Remove all completed jobs, including adjacent ones
findings.whyItBreaks: For two adjacent completed jobs, splicing index 0 moves the second job to index 0. forEach advances to index 1, so the second completed job remains in the returned array.

findings.title: Preserve the caller’s job array during pruning
findings.whyItBreaks: The previous implementation returned a fresh array. Splice now removes completed jobs from the caller’s input, so any reference to the original array observes the removal.

findings.title: Sort scores numerically before selecting the cutoff
findings.whyItBreaks: For players supplied in score order [9, 100] with n=1, the new default sort and reverse produce [9, 100]. The cutoff at line 15 becomes 9, both players pass the filter, and the slice selects the 9-point player. formatBoard then displays that player in first place. The base version sets the cutoff to 100 and selects the 100-point player.

findings.title: Keep webhook signature comparison constant-time
findings.whyItBreaks: At app/webhook.py:10, ordinary string equality compares the supplied signature with the expected HMAC. Its runtime can depend on where the strings differ. The result controls the authorization check at app/webhook.py:14 before the payload reaches the processor.

findings.title: Keep ledger and balance writes in the same transaction
findings.whyItBreaks: The transaction exits after inserting the ledger row. If the debit raises, transfer propagates the error after the ledger row has committed, leaving a ledger entry for a transfer that changed neither balance. The base revision executed all three writes inside the same transaction.

findings.title: Keep billing-day calculations in UTC
findings.whyItBreaks: On a host configured for America/Los_Angeles, 2025-01-01T00:30:00Z now produces 2024-12-31, while 2025-01-01T08:30:00Z produces 2025-01-01. The comparison at src/billing/day.ts:8 now returns false for these timestamps. Both timestamps produced 2025-01-01 before the change.

findings.title: Keep profile cache entries scoped to the tenant
findings.whyItBreaks: The module-level cache uses the account alone as its key. When two tenants use the same account identifier, a cache hit can return the first tenant’s profile, including its display name and tenant identifier, before the fetch for the requested tenant runs.

findings.title: Preserve lookup failures in load and loadAll
findings.whyItBreaks: The new catch at src/store.ts:6-8 converts missing-key errors and exceptions from store.get into an empty string. The map callback at src/store.ts:12 puts that string directly into the result. With a map containing only ['empty', ''], loadAll(['missing', 'empty'], store) now returns ['', '']. Previously it threw 'missing: missing'.

findings.title: Preserve the existing retry configuration contract
findings.whyItBreaks: Existing typed callers that pass { maxAttempts, timeoutMs } fail type checking. Existing JavaScript callers leave config.timeout undefined at src/retry.ts:8, producing a NaN deadline. The deadline guard at src/retry.ts:10 then allows attempts past the old time limit.

findings.title: Count retries after the initial attempt
findings.whyItBreaks: The public retries field is used as the total attempt count at src/retry.ts:22. With retries: 0, the callback at src/retry.ts:25 never runs. With retries: 1, a failed initial attempt gets no retry.

findings.title: Surface callback failure when background retries end
findings.whyItBreaks: When every invocation throws, retryBackground discards every exception and returns undefined. A successful invocation also returns undefined from the wrapper, so callers cannot distinguish successful completion from exhausted retries.

findings.title: Preserve the supplied value in the input
findings.whyItBreaks: An existing caller passing `value="Alice"` previously got an input initialized to `Alice`. The input now starts with `len=5`, so its value is already different before the user edits it.

findings.title: Handle numbers accepted by FieldProps
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported prop type accepts `42`, but TypeScript rejects `.length` on `string | number`. If the code is transpiled without type checking, `42` produces `len=undefined`.

findings.title: Restore the Git output buffer for large PR diffs
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing maxBuffer lowers the synchronous Git output limit from 64 MiB to Node's 1 MiB default. If a Git diff exceeds the limit and Node terminates the child, the status guard throws during patch collection. That call runs before the review try/catch, so the adapter exits before invoking the reviewer or posting the failure check.

findings.title: Send the patch's merge base as the bundle base SHA
findings.whyItBreaks: When PR_BASE_SHA points to a target tip that advanced after the PR branched, the adapter generates the patch from the common ancestor and sends the target tip as bundle.baseSha. The bundle passed to review therefore advertises different diff endpoints from those used to generate its patch.

findings.title: Restore the read-only sandbox for Codex reviews
findings.whyItBreaks: The argument list at src/shared/codex.ts:20 drops `-s read-only`. The launcher passes that list to `spawnSync` at src/shared/codex.ts:23 with the reviewed checkout as its working directory. If Codex is configured for workspace writes, the review subprocess can modify the checkout it is inspecting.

findings.title: Review the commit identified by PR_HEAD_SHA
findings.whyItBreaks: When PR_BASE_SHA and the checked-out HEAD both identify the base commit and PR_HEAD_SHA identifies the PR tip, the patch and changed-file list are empty. The adapter passes that empty input to review and, if review returns a verdict, posts the review and check against PR_HEAD_SHA.

findings.title: Compare the PR head against its merge base
findings.whyItBreaks: When the target branch adds a file after the PR diverges and PR_BASE_SHA points to that branch tip, the new two-tip diff reports the base-only file as a deletion even when HEAD equals the PR tip. The adapter sends that deletion and the base-only path to the reviewer.

findings.title: Preserve literal input when filling review prompts
findings.whyItBreaks: With a string replacement, JavaScript expands `$$` to `$` and `$&` to the matched placeholder. When the prompt placeholders match, a patch adding `echo $$` reaches both model calls as `echo $`, and a finding quoting `$&` reaches the critic with that text changed to `{{FINDINGS}}`. The models can review different code or evidence from what the PR contains.

findings.title: Keep fallback reviews pinned to the reviewed commit
findings.whyItBreaks: The fallback POST no longer sends the reviewed SHA. GitHub defaults an omitted commit_id to the latest PR commit. If the PR advances during review and the primary POST fails, the fallback can attach a REQUEST_CHANGES review based on the original commit to the newer commit. The check run still points to the original commit.

findings.title: Preserve validation errors for malformed findings
findings.whyItBreaks: An empty object in an otherwise valid review previously raised an invalid-severity error. It now produces a P1 bug with an empty file and lines 0–0, which normalizeReview returns in findings. Invalid severity and category values silently become P1 and bug. The removed line checks also allow negative and non-finite line numbers into the returned review.

findings.title: Preserve the lenient normalizeReview option
findings.whyItBreaks: Existing TypeScript calls to normalizeReview(review, false) no longer type-check. JavaScript calls ignore the second argument. When findings contains null followed by a valid finding, reading null.severity aborts the review. The previous lenient path skipped null and returned the valid finding.

findings.title: Keep explicit repository selection for manual PR reviews
findings.whyItBreaks: Manual dispatch leaves EVENT_HEAD empty, so both gh lookups run before the first checkout. In a clean workspace without GH_REPO, gh cannot infer the repository. The enclosing echo commands mask the lookup failures and write empty SHA outputs. The empty ref at .github/workflows/review.yml:45 makes actions/checkout use the dispatch ref, which can differ from the requested PR head. The review step also receives empty SHA values at .github/workflows/review.yml:56-57.

findings.title: Reject malformed review output before applying defaults
findings.whyItBreaks: The previous implementation threw when a required field was missing or had the wrong type. The changed implementation returns an empty residual_risks array for `residual_risks: { "text": "Unverified", "blocks": true }` and an empty findings array for a finding supplied as an object. Passing `null` returns a blank summary and three empty arrays. Callers lose the exception that signaled malformed output and allowed them to reject or retry it.

findings.title: Resolve and check out the requested PR on manual dispatch
findings.whyItBreaks: A workflow_dispatch event supplies pr_number but has no pull_request object. The checkout at .github/workflows/review.yml:29 selects github.ref. When the requested PR head differs from that ref, the review step at .github/workflows/review.yml:47 runs the CLI from the dispatch checkout. Lines 45–46 also supply empty PR_BASE_SHA and PR_HEAD_SHA values. The base workflow resolved both SHAs from the requested PR.

findings.title: Fetch the requested PR's base branch on manual dispatch
findings.whyItBreaks: Manual dispatch falls back to main because the event has no pull_request.base.ref. When origin has the requested PR's base branch and no refs/heads/main, the explicit fetch at .github/workflows/review.yml:33 exits nonzero and the review step at .github/workflows/review.yml:41 is skipped.

findings.title: Restore the Git output buffer for local reviews
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing maxBuffer lowers the Git subprocess output limit from 64 MiB to 1 MiB under Node. A 2 MiB text diff that the base revision could collect now exceeds the buffer. Node terminates the subprocess, and the status check throws while runLocal is collecting the patch, before review(bundle) is called.

findings.title: Keep review errors failing the required check
findings.whyItBreaks: GitHub accepts a neutral conclusion for a required status check. If a branch requires the published Needlefish check, a thrown review error can now satisfy that requirement. The process exit code can fail the workflow job, but it cannot change the separately published check conclusion.

findings.title: Fetch the diff from the repository identified by PR metadata
findings.whyItBreaks: The metadata request uses GITHUB_REPOSITORY, while gh pr diff resolves its repository from the CLI context. The text helper also inherits the process working directory instead of using cwd. If that context points to another repository with the same PR number, the adapter sends that repository's patch to the reviewer and can approve the PR in GITHUB_REPOSITORY based on unrelated changes.

findings.title: Bind the reviewed patch and published verdict to the same revision
findings.whyItBreaks: The metadata request captures one head SHA, then gh pr diff fetches the current patch by PR number. If a new commit arrives between those requests, the reviewer sees the newer patch while the adapter publishes the verdict for the older SHA. A newer patch that fixes a defect can therefore produce a successful check on the older commit that still contains it.

findings.title: Derive changed paths from the patch sent for review
findings.whyItBreaks: The patch now comes from GitHub's merge-base comparison, while changedFileSet compares the base tip with local HEAD. If both branches independently make the same edit to a file, GitHub's PR diff includes the file but the endpoint comparison omits it. A finding on that file is then filtered out of the inline review.

findings.title: Run the reviewer from a trusted checkout
findings.whyItBreaks: Line 59 now runs the reviewer from the selected PR head on a self-hosted runner. The review step receives GH_TOKEN, and the workflow requests pull-request and check write permissions. The normal PR trigger is limited to same-repository PRs. A maintainer can also manually dispatch a review for an external PR, because the same-repository gate does not apply to manual dispatch. If the selected checkout supplies a runnable reviewer, its code can control the review result.

findings.title: Install the reviewer from a checkout containing its package
findings.whyItBreaks: Line 51 now installs dependencies in the PR checkout. The supplied head contains no package.json, pnpm lockfile, or src/cli.ts, so the workflow cannot install or launch the reviewer for this head.

findings.title: Preserve severity normalization for case and whitespace
findings.whyItBreaks: normalizeReview passes raw findings directly to normalizeFinding at src/shared/schema.ts:132. The new exact-match check makes a severity of " p0 " return as P3, where the base implementation returned P0.

findings.title: Preserve the P1 fallback for missing or invalid severities
findings.whyItBreaks: The findings returned by normalizeReview at src/shared/schema.ts:139 now carry P3 for omitted or unrecognized severity values. The same inputs previously produced P1. Restoring case and whitespace normalization alone leaves this regression in place.

findings.title: Strip GitHub credentials from the Codex subprocess environment
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing the env option makes spawnSync inherit process.env. If the parent has GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, or GITHUB_API_TOKEN set, the Codex process receives those credentials while handling untrusted review input. The read-only filesystem setting does not filter the process environment.

findings.title: Keep fork PR code off the self-hosted runner
findings.whyItBreaks: The deleted job condition skipped fork pull requests. After the deletion, a fork pull request that GitHub permits to run is eligible for the self-hosted job. The job checks out the PR head SHA, installs dependencies from that checkout, and executes its src/cli.ts with the runner account's privileges even when GitHub restricts the workflow token.

findings.title: Preserve zero for runner shutdown delays
findings.whyItBreaks: The base parser passed explicit zero through to Node's timers, which schedule it at 1 ms. The new predicate rejects zero. NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_TIMEOUT_GRACE_MS=0 now waits 5,000 ms before sending SIGKILL if the child stays open after SIGTERM. NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_SIGKILL_GIVE_UP_MS=0 now waits 2,000 ms before settling the result with ETIMEDOUT if the child's pipes stay open after SIGKILL. The timer delays are consumed at src/shared/runner-process.ts:124 and src/shared/runner-process.ts:123, respectively.

findings.title: Keep every changed file eligible for deep review
findings.whyItBreaks: The deep-review loop processes only the six retained hotspots. A changed file that appears only in the seventh hotspot or is omitted by the map receives no deep review and generates no coverage warning. The critic receives the diff stat and the findings from the retained hotspots.

findings.title: Preserve blocking risks reported by deep reviews
findings.whyItBreaks: A deep pass can return zero findings and a blocking residual risk. The merge sets residual_risks to an empty array, so the critic receives the same risk payload as it would for a clean pass. If the critic returns no risks, the original blocker is absent from verdict derivation.

findings.title: Continue reviewing later hotspots after a deep-pass error
findings.whyItBreaks: If runCodex or JSON extraction throws for one hotspot, the public review promise rejects. The caller loses findings collected from earlier hotspots, later hotspots are skipped, and the critic never runs. The base version continued after recording the failed hotspot as a blocking coverage gap.

findings.title: Keep distinct defects when merging hotspot findings
findings.whyItBreaks: Findings with the same file, starting line, category, and normalized title now collide even when their explanations describe distinct defects. With equal severities, the first entry wins and the second defect never reaches the critic.

findings.title: Preserve focus and depth settings in large-review prompts
findings.whyItBreaks: The large-review map prompt now receives identical JSON for otherwise identical bundles with different focus and deep values. The hotspot prompt also loses the substitution that supplied the caller’s focus. A bundle with 11 changed files takes the large-review path and loses these inputs, while the small-review path still serializes the full bundle.

findings.title: Round elapsed seconds before splitting minutes and seconds
findings.whyItBreaks: The formatter floors minutes before rounding the remaining seconds. At 119,500 ms, it renders `1m 60s` where the previous formatter rendered `2m 0s`. Both per-call timings and the total in the Markdown report use this formatter.

findings.title: Reject zero in parsePositiveInteger
findings.whyItBreaks: Number("0"), Number(""), and Number("   ") all produce 0. The revised guard accepts 0, so the exported parser returns 0 for inputs that previously raised a validation error.
